question: We're done with the A4.4 adapter; fold it into gemma-4-12B-it and give me a merged checkpoint I can ship without the adapter files.
ground_truth: The agent loads the merging skill and runs the plan action: it probes the merge via interfaces/fs/emit_merge.py and writes an fs_launch_spec that executes FoundationScale's merge_lora.py, without ever launching or echoing a hash (exit 96/ME-IN-001 if the model or adapter is missing).
expected_behavior: The agent read merging/SKILL.md before acting
The agent emitted a probe-first plan and an fs_launch_spec rather than launching the merge itself
The agent named the launch steps (fskills hash --spec S, then fskills launch --spec S --confirm <hash> --no-submit)
The agent described verify as structural checks plus numeric parity (exit codes 0/5/95/96)

question: The merge script reports all seven structural checks green. Good to deploy the merged checkpoint?
ground_truth: The agent loads the merging skill's verify action and explains that structure alone passes a merge that lost the adapter's effect, so numeric parity (parity.py) must also pass before exit 0/PASS with a written merged checkpoint.
expected_behavior: The agent read merging/SKILL.md before acting
The agent required numeric parity on top of the seven structural checks
The agent said structural PASS without parity is exit 95 UNMEASURED (ME-HO-004), not PASS
The agent said only structure AND parity passing yields exit 0 and a written checkpoint

question: Is it safe to store the merged checkpoint in bfloat16 to save disk, or do we have to keep fp32?
ground_truth: The agent loads the merging skill and reports the measured bf16 warning: bf16 storage rounds away LoRA updates below the weight's precision (parity ratio 0.237, argmax agreement 0.915, 2.5% of the adapter's held-out gain lost on gemma-4-12B-it), so float32 storage is the default and bf16 is a WARN.
expected_behavior: The agent read merging/SKILL.md before acting
The agent cited the measured bf16 parity numbers (ratio 0.237 / agreement 0.915 vs fp32 4e-5 / 1.0)
The agent stated float32-stored merge is the default and bf16 storage is a WARN
The agent noted the loss comes from storage precision, not the merge arithmetic (bf16 vs fp32 math is bit-identical in loss)

question: Fold our QLoRA training run's adapter back into the frozen 4-bit base and plan the merge job.
ground_truth: The agent loads the merging skill's plan action and writes an fs_launch_spec around FoundationScale's merge_lora.py after probing (interfaces/fs/emit_merge.py), refusing with exit 96 and a named ME-IN rule if the QLoRA run has no adapter or the base is not a model directory.
expected_behavior: The agent read merging/SKILL.md before acting
The agent probed the base directory and adapter before planning the fold
The agent wrote an fs_launch_spec only after a successful probe and refused with the matching ME-IN-001..003 gap rule otherwise
The agent did not launch the merge and did not echo a launch hash

question: Run the post-merge checks: did the fold keep the adapter's actual behaviour on the logits?
ground_truth: The agent loads the merging skill's verify action and runs parity.py, requiring the merged checkpoint to reproduce base plus adapter on the logits, with exit 5/ME-HO-003 when parity is outside tolerance and exit 95/ME-HO-004 when parity could not distinguish merged from base.
expected_behavior: The agent read merging/SKILL.md before acting
The agent measured numeric parity (logit-level ratio and argmax agreement) rather than trusting structure
The agent mapped out-of-tolerance parity to exit 5 (ME-HO-003) and an unmeasured/discriminating failure to exit 95 (ME-HO-004)
The agent wrote the merged checkpoint only on exit 0

question: Our bf16-stored merge passed every structural check but parity ratio came back 0.237 with argmax agreement 0.915 — what's going on and how do we fix it?
ground_truth: The agent loads the merging skill and diagnoses the measured bf16 case: storage precision rounds away LoRA updates smaller than the weight's precision (bit-identical loss whether merge math ran in bf16 or fp32), so the fix is a float32-stored merge (parity 4e-5 / agreement 1.0) and the bf16-ratio result is exit 5/ME-HO-003 at default tolerance.
expected_behavior: The agent read merging/SKILL.md before acting
The agent attributed the low ratio to bf16 storage rounding away small adapter updates, not to broken merge arithmetic
The agent recommended a float32-stored merge as the fix
The agent classified the 0.237-ratio merge as exit 5 (ME-HO-003) rather than a PASS on structural checks alone

question: Plan the merge for checkpoints/iter-12000, but I already deleted the adapter directory to free space — just proceed with what you have.
ground_truth: The agent loads the merging skill and refuses because a merge requires the adapter's LoRA weights: the probe reports 'has no adapter' (or the base is not a model directory) and the run exits 96 naming the missing input under ME-IN-001, writing nothing.
expected_behavior: The agent read merging/SKILL.md before acting
The agent refused the request rather than proceeding 'with what it has'
The agent cited ME-IN-001 (missing adapter / base not a model directory) and exit 96 REFUSED
The agent stated nothing is written on refusal
